NF-ToN-IoT v2 — Full-File Dataset Audit¶

Scope: every row of NF-ToN-IoT-v2.csv (16,940,496 flows, 45 columns), not a head sample.

This notebook is the v2 counterpart to the v3 temporal audit. It measures:

  • full-file integrity, label consistency, missing/inf values, and extreme values;
  • key-based and full-row duplicate groups, including their distribution by class;
  • exact per-class counts, host cardinality, protocol and destination-port structure;
  • full-file per-class statistics for all 41 numeric features;
  • full-file correlation structure and class-separability statistics;
  • a deterministic per-class sample used only for quantiles and plots, with uniqueness verified.

Critical limitation: v2 has no timestamps and no inter-arrival-time fields. Temporal ordering, attack-block structure, and fixed-time/fixed-flow graph-window feasibility cannot be measured in v2. Those questions belong to the v3 audit. V2 is a full cross-sectional/class audit, not a temporal one.

Stage 1 — Full-file integrity and duplicate structure¶

1A. Schema and feature groups¶

The CSV has 45 columns: 2 IP identity columns, 41 numeric flow features, Label (binary), and Attack (class name).

# 1B. Full-file integrity pass (all rows), plus file-order diagnostics.
n_total = 0
label_counts = Counter()
attack_counts = Counter()
unexpected_attacks = Counter()
label_attack_mismatch = 0

missing_cells = Counter()
n_nan_num = 0
n_inf_num = 0
feat_neg = np.zeros(len(NUM_COLS), dtype=np.int64)
feat_gt = np.zeros(len(NUM_COLS), dtype=np.int64)
feat_min = np.full(len(NUM_COLS), np.inf)
feat_max = np.full(len(NUM_COLS), -np.inf)

bad_protocol = 0
bad_src_port = 0
bad_dst_port = 0
flow_dur_zero = 0
dur_dir_zero_flow_pos = 0
flow_lt_maxdir = 0
flow_gt_10x_dir = 0

K = len(CLASS_NAMES)
class_rows = np.zeros(K, dtype=np.int64)
first_row = np.full(K, -1, dtype=np.int64)
last_row = np.full(K, -1, dtype=np.int64)
run_count = np.zeros(K, dtype=np.int64)
longest_run = np.zeros(K, dtype=np.int64)
prev_code = -1
row_offset = 0

for ch in pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, chunksize=CHUNK):
    n = len(ch)
    n_total += n
    lab = ch['Label'].to_numpy(dtype=np.int8)
    atk = ch['Attack'].to_numpy()

    label_counts.update(lab.tolist())
    attack_counts.update(atk.tolist())
    for name in np.unique(atk):
        if name not in class_to_code:
            unexpected_attacks[str(name)] += 1
    label_attack_mismatch += int(np.count_nonzero((lab == 0) != (atk == 'Benign')))

    missing_cells.update(ch.isna().sum().to_dict())

    X = ch[NUM_COLS].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    n_nan_num += int(np.isnan(X).sum())
    n_inf_num += int(np.isinf(X).sum())
    feat_neg += np.count_nonzero(X < 0, axis=0)
    feat_gt += np.count_nonzero(X > 1e12, axis=0)
    Xf = np.where(np.isfinite(X), X, np.nan)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        cmin = np.nanmin(Xf, axis=0)
        cmax = np.nanmax(Xf, axis=0)
    feat_min = np.fmin(feat_min, cmin)
    feat_max = np.fmax(feat_max, cmax)

    d = ch['FLOW_DURATION_MILLISECONDS'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    di = ch['DURATION_IN'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    do = ch['DURATION_OUT'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    flow_dur_zero += int(np.count_nonzero(d == 0))
    dur_dir_zero_flow_pos += int(np.count_nonzero((d > 0) & (di + do == 0)))
    flow_lt_maxdir += int(np.count_nonzero(d < np.maximum(di, do)))
    flow_gt_10x_dir += int(np.count_nonzero((d > 0) & (d > 10 * (di + do))))

    proto = ch['PROTOCOL'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    sport = ch['L4_SRC_PORT'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    dport = ch['L4_DST_PORT'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    bad_protocol += int(np.count_nonzero((proto < 0) | (proto > 255)))
    bad_src_port += int(np.count_nonzero((sport < 0) | (sport > 65535)))
    bad_dst_port += int(np.count_nonzero((dport < 0) | (dport > 65535)))

    codes = pd.Series(atk).map(class_to_code).fillna(-1).to_numpy(dtype=np.int64)
    valid = codes >= 0
    class_rows += np.bincount(codes[valid], minlength=K)

    for c in range(K):
        idx = np.flatnonzero(codes == c)
        if len(idx):
            if first_row[c] < 0:
                first_row[c] = row_offset + int(idx[0])
            last_row[c] = row_offset + int(idx[-1])

    changes = np.empty(n, dtype=bool)
    changes[0] = (prev_code != codes[0])
    if n > 1:
        changes[1:] = codes[1:] != codes[:-1]
    starts = np.flatnonzero(changes)
    if len(starts):
        rc = codes[starts]
        ends = np.r_[starts[1:], n]
        rl = ends - starts
        v = rc >= 0
        np.add.at(run_count, rc[v], 1)
        np.maximum.at(longest_run, rc[v], rl[v])
    prev_code = int(codes[-1])
    row_offset += n

N_FILE_ROWS = int(n_total)

print('Rows                    :', f'{N_FILE_ROWS:,}')
print('Columns                 :', len(all_cols))
print('Label counts (0/1)      :', dict(label_counts))
print('Attack counts           :', dict(sorted(attack_counts.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])))
print('Label/Attack mismatch   :', label_attack_mismatch)
print('Unexpected attack names :', dict(unexpected_attacks))
print('Missing cells           :', int(sum(missing_cells.values())))
print('NaN in numeric features :', n_nan_num)
print('Inf in numeric features :', n_inf_num)
print('Negative numeric values :', int(feat_neg.sum()))
print('Values > 1e12           :', int(feat_gt.sum()))
print('Bad protocol values     :', bad_protocol)
print('Bad source-port values  :', bad_src_port)
print('Bad destination-port values:', bad_dst_port)
print('Flow duration == 0      :', flow_dur_zero, f'({flow_dur_zero/N_FILE_ROWS*100:.3f}%)')
print('Duration dirs 0 but flow > 0:', dur_dir_zero_flow_pos)
print('Flow duration < max(dir):', flow_lt_maxdir, f'({flow_lt_maxdir/N_FILE_ROWS*100:.3f}%)')
print('Flow duration > 10x dirs:', flow_gt_10x_dir, f'({flow_gt_10x_dir/N_FILE_ROWS*100:.3f}%)')
if missing_cells:
    print('Columns with missing cells:', dict(missing_cells))
print()
order_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Class': CLASS_NAMES,
    'Rows': class_rows,
    'First_row': first_row,
    'Last_row': last_row,
    'Contiguous_runs': run_count,
    'Runs_per_row': np.round(run_count / np.maximum(class_rows, 1), 4),
    'Longest_run': longest_run,
})
print('File-order structure (no timestamps, so row order is the only ordering available):')
print(order_df.to_string(index=False))

# 1C. Duplicate audit: key-based and full-row, globally and per class.
KEY_COLS = ['IPV4_SRC_ADDR', 'L4_SRC_PORT', 'IPV4_DST_ADDR', 'L4_DST_PORT', 'PROTOCOL',
            'IN_BYTES', 'OUT_BYTES', 'IN_PKTS', 'OUT_PKTS', 'FLOW_DURATION_MILLISECONDS']

def scan_duplicate_hashes(usecols, hash_cols, full_row=False):
    hash_lists = {name: [] for name in CLASS_NAMES}
    for ch in pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, chunksize=CHUNK, usecols=usecols):
        atk = ch['Attack'].to_numpy()
        for name in CLASS_NAMES:
            m = atk == name
            if m.any():
                sub = ch.loc[m] if full_row else ch.loc[m, hash_cols]
                h = pd.util.hash_pandas_object(sub, index=False).to_numpy(dtype=np.uint64)
                hash_lists[name].append(h)
    return hash_lists

def duplicate_summary(hash_lists):
    per_class = {}
    all_parts = []
    for name in CLASS_NAMES:
        parts = hash_lists[name]
        if not parts:
            per_class[name] = (0, 0, 0)
            continue
        h = np.concatenate(parts)
        all_parts.append(h)
        h.sort()
        mask = h[1:] == h[:-1]
        runs = np.diff(np.flatnonzero(np.concatenate(([True], ~mask, [True]))))
        per_class[name] = (len(h), int(np.count_nonzero(runs > 1)),
                           int((runs[runs > 1] - 1).sum()))
    h = np.concatenate(all_parts)
    h.sort()
    mask = h[1:] == h[:-1]
    runs = np.diff(np.flatnonzero(np.concatenate(([True], ~mask, [True]))))
    global_stats = (len(h), int(np.count_nonzero(runs > 1)),
                    int((runs[runs > 1] - 1).sum()))
    return per_class, global_stats

key_lists = scan_duplicate_hashes(KEY_COLS + ['Attack'], KEY_COLS, full_row=False)
key_per, key_global = duplicate_summary(key_lists)
del key_lists
gc.collect()

row_lists = scan_duplicate_hashes(None, None, full_row=True)
row_per, row_global = duplicate_summary(row_lists)
del row_lists
gc.collect()

dup_rows = []
for name in CLASS_NAMES:
    kr, kg, kred = key_per[name]
    rr, rg, rred = row_per[name]
    dup_rows.append([name, int(class_rows[class_to_code[name]]),
                     kg, kred, round(100 * kred / max(kr, 1), 4),
                     rg, rred, round(100 * rred / max(rr, 1), 4)])
dup_df = pd.DataFrame(dup_rows, columns=['Class', 'Rows',
                                         'Key_dup_groups', 'Key_redundant_rows', 'Key_redundant_pct',
                                         'Fullrow_dup_groups', 'Fullrow_redundant_rows', 'Fullrow_redundant_pct'])
print('--- Key-based duplicates (10 flow-identifying columns) ---')
print(f'Global groups          : {key_global[1]:,}')
print(f'Global redundant rows  : {key_global[2]:,} ({key_global[2]/N_FILE_ROWS*100:.4f}% of file)')
print()
print('--- Full-row exact duplicates (all 45 columns) ---')
print(f'Global groups          : {row_global[1]:,}')
print(f'Global redundant rows  : {row_global[2]:,} ({row_global[2]/N_FILE_ROWS*100:.4f}% of file)')
print()
print(dup_df.to_string(index=False))
print()
print('Note: key-based duplicate groups can be shared across classes; full-row duplicates')
print('include Label and Attack, so their per-class group counts are class-local.')

Stage 2 — Exact class distribution and host/service structure¶

Key data-quality finding from Stage 1¶

  • FLOW_DURATION_MILLISECONDS is zero for 81.539% of all 16,940,496 rows, and every nonzero flow duration is more than 10× the sum of DURATION_IN and DURATION_OUT. This is consistent with the directional duration fields being recorded in different units (likely seconds vs milliseconds), so the fields must not be treated as interchangeable.
  • 2,822,214 rows have positive flow duration but both directional durations equal zero.
  • 1,167 numeric values exceed 1e12; these are concentrated in derived rate fields and require log-scale/robust statistics.

2A. Class distribution (full file)¶

dist_rows = []
attack_total = sum(int(attack_counts[a]) for a in ATTACK_ORDER)
for name in CLASS_NAMES:
    n = int(class_rows[class_to_code[name]])
    dist_rows.append([name, n, round(100 * n / N_FILE_ROWS, 4),
                      round(100 * n / attack_total, 4) if name != 'Benign' else 0.0])

# 2B. Full-file host cardinality and protocol/destination-port structure.
host_cols = ['Attack', 'IPV4_SRC_ADDR', 'IPV4_DST_ADDR', 'L4_DST_PORT', 'PROTOCOL']
src_sets = [set() for _ in CLASS_NAMES]
dst_sets = [set() for _ in CLASS_NAMES]
proto_ct = [Counter() for _ in CLASS_NAMES]
dport_ct = [Counter() for _ in CLASS_NAMES]

for ch in pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, chunksize=CHUNK, usecols=host_cols):
    atk = ch['Attack'].to_numpy()
    src = ch['IPV4_SRC_ADDR'].to_numpy()
    dst = ch['IPV4_DST_ADDR'].to_numpy()
    proto = ch['PROTOCOL'].to_numpy()
    dport = ch['L4_DST_PORT'].to_numpy()
    for c, name in enumerate(CLASS_NAMES):
        m = atk == name
        if m.any():
            src_sets[c].update(src[m].tolist())
            dst_sets[c].update(dst[m].tolist())
            proto_ct[c].update(proto[m].tolist())
            dport_ct[c].update(dport[m].tolist())

host_rows = []
for c, name in enumerate(CLASS_NAMES):
    n = int(class_rows[c])
    top_proto = proto_ct[c].most_common(1)[0] if proto_ct[c] else (None, 0)
    top_port = dport_ct[c].most_common(1)[0] if dport_ct[c] else (None, 0)
    host_rows.append([name, n, len(src_sets[c]), len(dst_sets[c]),
                      top_proto[0], round(100 * top_proto[1] / max(n, 1), 2),
                      top_port[0], round(100 * top_port[1] / max(n, 1), 2)])
host_df = pd.DataFrame(host_rows, columns=['Class', 'Rows', 'Unique_src_IPs', 'Unique_dst_IPs',
                                           'Top_protocol', 'Top_protocol_pct',
                                           'Top_dst_port', 'Top_dst_port_pct'])
print(host_df.to_string(index=False))

def jac(a, b):
    if not a or not b:
        return 0.0
    return len(a & b) / len(a | b)

JS = np.array([[jac(src_sets[i], src_sets[j]) for j in range(K)] for i in range(K)])
JD = np.array([[jac(dst_sets[i], dst_sets[j]) for j in range(K)] for i in range(K)])

Stage 3 — Full-file per-class feature statistics¶

3A. Exact full-file aggregates for all 41 numeric features¶

The pass below accumulates, for every class and every numeric feature:

  • row count, minimum, maximum, zero share, negative count, and share above 1e12;
  • exact sums of raw values (clipped only at 1e300 to prevent overflow);
  • exact sums of log1p(x) and log1p(x)^2, used for stable means/standard deviations;
  • exact cross-products of log1p(x), used for the full-file correlation matrix;
  • a deterministic per-class reservoir of raw rows for quantiles and plots only.

The quantiles and plots are sample-based because exact quantiles would require storing the full column. Everything else in this stage is computed from all rows.

The complete 410-row table (10 classes × 41 features) is written to figures/v2_per_class_feature_stats.csv; the next cell displays only the decision-relevant subset.

In [7]:
F = len(NUM_COLS)
K = len(CLASS_NAMES)

n_by = np.zeros(K, dtype=np.int64)
sum_raw = np.zeros((K, F), dtype=np.float64)
sum_log = np.zeros((K, F), dtype=np.float64)
sumsq_log = np.zeros((K, F), dtype=np.float64)
cross_log = np.zeros((K, F, F), dtype=np.float64)
vmin = np.full((K, F), np.inf)
vmax = np.full((K, F), -np.inf)
zero_ct = np.zeros((K, F), dtype=np.int64)
neg_ct = np.zeros((K, F), dtype=np.int64)
huge_ct = np.zeros((K, F), dtype=np.int64)

SAMPLE_CAPS = np.array([50_000] + [20_000] * (K - 1), dtype=np.int64)
res_X = [np.empty((int(SAMPLE_CAPS[c]), F), dtype=np.float64) for c in range(K)]
res_ids = [np.empty(int(SAMPLE_CAPS[c]), dtype=np.int64) for c in range(K)]
res_n = np.zeros(K, dtype=np.int64)
seen = np.zeros(K, dtype=np.int64)
SAMPLE_SEED = 0
rng = np.random.default_rng(SAMPLE_SEED)
row_offset = 0

for ch in pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, chunksize=CHUNK, usecols=['Attack'] + NUM_COLS):
    atk = ch['Attack'].to_numpy()
    codes = pd.Series(atk).map(class_to_code).fillna(-1).to_numpy(dtype=np.int64)
    X = ch[NUM_COLS].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    X = np.nan_to_num(X, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    Xc = np.clip(X, 0, None)
    L = np.log1p(Xc)
    chunk_ids = np.arange(row_offset, row_offset + len(ch), dtype=np.int64)
    row_offset += len(ch)

    for c in range(K):
        m = codes == c
        n = int(m.sum())
        if n == 0:
            continue
        Xm = X[m]
        Lm = L[m]

        n_by[c] += n
        sum_raw[c] += np.minimum(Xm, 1e300).sum(axis=0)
        sum_log[c] += Lm.sum(axis=0)
        sumsq_log[c] += (Lm * Lm).sum(axis=0)
        cross_log[c] += Lm.T @ Lm
        vmin[c] = np.minimum(vmin[c], Xm.min(axis=0))
        vmax[c] = np.maximum(vmax[c], Xm.max(axis=0))
        zero_ct[c] += np.count_nonzero(Xm == 0, axis=0)
        neg_ct[c] += np.count_nonzero(Xm < 0, axis=0)
        huge_ct[c] += np.count_nonzero(Xm > 1e12, axis=0)

        seen_before = int(seen[c])
        seen[c] += n
        cap = int(SAMPLE_CAPS[c])
        fill_end = min(seen_before + n, cap)
        if seen_before < fill_end:
            k = fill_end - seen_before
            res_X[c][seen_before:fill_end] = Xm[:k]
            res_ids[c][seen_before:fill_end] = chunk_ids[m][:k]

        replace_start = max(seen_before, cap)
        if seen_before + n > replace_start:
            positions = np.arange(replace_start, seen_before + n, dtype=np.int64)
            local = positions - seen_before
            probs = cap / (positions.astype(float) + 1.0)
            do_replace = rng.random(len(positions)) < probs
            if do_replace.any():
                slots = rng.integers(0, cap, size=int(do_replace.sum()))
                res_X[c][slots] = Xm[local[do_replace]]
                res_ids[c][slots] = chunk_ids[m][local[do_replace]]

    if row_offset % 5_000_000 < CHUNK:
        print('scanned', f'{row_offset:,}', 'rows ...')

for c in range(K):
    res_n[c] = min(int(seen[c]), int(SAMPLE_CAPS[c]))

mean_log = sum_log / n_by[:, None]
var_log = np.clip(sumsq_log / n_by[:, None] - mean_log ** 2, 0, None)
std_log = np.sqrt(var_log)
mean_raw = sum_raw / n_by[:, None]

q50 = np.full((K, F), np.nan)
q95 = np.full((K, F), np.nan)
q99 = np.full((K, F), np.nan)
for c in range(K):
    arr = res_X[c][:res_n[c]]
    q50[c], q95[c], q99[c] = np.percentile(arr, [50, 95, 99], axis=0)

stats_rows = []
for c, name in enumerate(CLASS_NAMES):
    for j, feat in enumerate(NUM_COLS):
        stats_rows.append({
            'Class': name,
            'Feature': feat,
            'Rows': int(n_by[c]),
            'Min': vmin[c, j],
            'Max': vmax[c, j],
            'Mean_raw_clipped': mean_raw[c, j],
            'Mean_log1p': mean_log[c, j],
            'Std_log1p': std_log[c, j],
            'Zero_pct': 100 * zero_ct[c, j] / n_by[c],
            'Negative_rows': int(neg_ct[c, j]),
            'GT_1e12_pct': 100 * huge_ct[c, j] / n_by[c],
            'P50_sample': q50[c, j],
            'P95_sample': q95[c, j],
            'P99_sample': q99[c, j],
        })
stats_df = pd.DataFrame(stats_rows)
stats_path = os.path.join(FIG_DIR, 'v2_per_class_feature_stats.csv')
stats_df.to_csv(stats_path, index=False)

print()
print('Full per-class feature table:', stats_df.shape, 'rows x columns')
print('Saved:', stats_path)
print('Sample seed:', SAMPLE_SEED)
print('Reservoir sizes:', dict(zip(CLASS_NAMES, res_n.tolist())))
print('Unique sampled row IDs:', sum(len(np.unique(res_ids[c][:res_n[c]])) for c in range(K)))

# 3C. Full-file correlation of log1p(feature), plus the strongest pairs.
mean_global = sum_log.sum(axis=0) / N_FILE_ROWS
cross_global = cross_log.sum(axis=0)
cov_global = cross_global / N_FILE_ROWS - np.outer(mean_global, mean_global)
std_global = np.sqrt(np.clip(np.diag(cov_global), 0, None))
denom = np.outer(std_global, std_global)
corr = np.divide(cov_global, denom, out=np.zeros_like(cov_global), where=denom > 0)
np.fill_diagonal(corr, 1.0)
corr = np.clip(corr, -1, 1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 15))
sns.heatmap(corr, xticklabels=NUM_COLS, yticklabels=NUM_COLS, cmap='RdBu_r',
            center=0, vmin=-1, vmax=1, ax=ax, cbar_kws={'label': 'Pearson r'})
ax.set_title('NF-ToN-IoT v2: full-file correlation of log1p(feature)')
ax.set_xlabel('Feature')
ax.set_ylabel('Feature')
plt.xticks(rotation=90, fontsize=6)
plt.yticks(fontsize=6)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIG_DIR, 'fig_v2_corr_log1p.png'), dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()
print('Saved', os.path.join(FIG_DIR, 'fig_v2_corr_log1p.png'))

pairs = []
for i in range(len(NUM_COLS)):
    for j in range(i + 1, len(NUM_COLS)):
        pairs.append((abs(corr[i, j]), corr[i, j], NUM_COLS[i], NUM_COLS[j]))
pairs.sort(reverse=True)
print()
print('Strongest absolute correlations (full file):')
for ab, r, a, b in pairs[:20]:
    print(f'  {a:28s} vs {b:28s} r={r:+.3f}')
pd.DataFrame(corr, index=NUM_COLS, columns=NUM_COLS).to_csv(
    os.path.join(FIG_DIR, 'v2_corr_log1p.csv'))

Stage 4 — Class separability¶

4A. Standardized mean difference on log1p features (full file)¶

For each attack class, the standardized mean difference (SMD) compares its log1p feature mean with Benign using the pooled log-scale standard deviation. This is computed from all rows, not from the sample.

# 4B. Deterministic per-class sample, sample integrity, and sample-based AUC/plots.
sample_parts = []
for c, name in enumerate(CLASS_NAMES):
    n = int(res_n[c])
    part = pd.DataFrame(res_X[c][:n], columns=NUM_COLS)
    part.insert(0, '_row_id', res_ids[c][:n])
    part['Class'] = name
    sample_parts.append(part)
sample_df = pd.concat(sample_parts, ignore_index=True)

print('--- Sample integrity ---')
print('Sample rows              :', f'{len(sample_df):,}')
print('Unique source-row IDs    :', f'{sample_df["_row_id"].nunique():,}')
print('Duplicated source-row IDs:', f'{int(sample_df["_row_id"].duplicated().sum()):,}')
print()
print(sample_df['Class'].value_counts().loc[CLASS_NAMES].to_string())

from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

sample_X = {name: sample_df[sample_df['Class'] == name][NUM_COLS].to_numpy()
            for name in CLASS_NAMES}
auc = np.full((len(NUM_COLS), len(ATTACK_ORDER)), np.nan)
for j, a in enumerate(ATTACK_ORDER):
    Xa = sample_X[a]
    Xb = sample_X['Benign']
    y = np.r_[np.ones(len(Xa)), np.zeros(len(Xb))]
    for i, feat in enumerate(NUM_COLS):
        s = np.r_[Xa[:, i], Xb[:, i]]
        if np.std(s) > 0:
            auc[i, j] = roc_auc_score(y, s)
auc_df = pd.DataFrame(auc, index=NUM_COLS, columns=ATTACK_ORDER)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 13))
sns.heatmap(auc_df, cmap='viridis', vmin=0.5, vmax=1.0, ax=ax,
            cbar_kws={'label': 'AUC (Benign vs attack)'})
ax.set_title('NF-ToN-IoT v2: sample-based AUC by feature and attack')
ax.set_xlabel('Attack class')
ax.set_ylabel('Feature')

Stage 5 — Summary¶

All counts, duplicate statistics, per-class feature aggregates, correlation, SMD, host cardinality, and service mix above are full-file measurements. The per-class reservoir is used only for quantiles (P50/P95/P99), AUC, and boxplots; it is deterministic with a recorded seed and its source-row IDs are unique.

Limitations specific to v2¶

  1. No timestamps or inter-arrival times. v2 cannot be used to measure attack ordering, capture-period confounding, attack-block structure, fixed-time window occupancy, or fixed-flow window spans. Those questions require v3.
  2. File order is interleaved. The full-file run count per class is large relative to its row count, so CSV row order is not a valid substitute for a timestamp.
  3. Derived rate features contain extreme values. SRC_TO_DST_SECOND_BYTES and DST_TO_SRC_SECOND_BYTES reach values near 1e305; the audit therefore reports log-scale statistics and flags the >1e12 share instead of relying on raw means.
  4. Quantiles, AUC, and boxplots are sample-based. The sample is deterministic (default_rng(0)), stratified by class, and verified unique. Exact full-file aggregates are reported separately.
  5. No flow-end consistency check is possible. v2 has duration fields but no FLOW_END_MILLISECONDS, so end >= start and duration arithmetic cannot be verified as in v3.
  6. Do not combine v2 and v3. They have different columns and v2 lacks the temporal fields; v3 remains the primary temporal audit.
  7. Duplicates are measured, not removed. Deletion would need a separate decision and must be applied consistently before task construction.
  8. Duration fields are not directly comparable. FLOW_DURATION_MILLISECONDS is zero for 81.539% of rows, and every nonzero value exceeds 10× DURATION_IN + DURATION_OUT; this suggests a unit mismatch (flow duration in ms, directional durations likely seconds). Reconcile units before using duration as a feature.

Bottom line¶

V2 is now audited at full-file scale, with per-class tables for all numeric features, exact duplicate-group counts, host/service structure, correlation, and separability. It is suitable as a cross-sectional comparison dataset and as a source of per-class feature evidence.

It is not a substitute for the v3 temporal audit. The central TRENCH-IDS question about attack ordering and scenario confounding can only be answered with v3 (or another timestamped dataset). Task construction remains blocked until the v3 confounding decision is made.
